title: Dynamic request sculpting — personal product brainstorming
body:
Top-level idea
---------------
Make a lightweight, runtime layer that can "sculpt" individual incoming requests to meet a per-request objective (latency, cost, quality, privacy). Not a full model selector service (though could integrate), more like per-request transformations + routing hints + progressive fidelity controls applied as a short pipeline before sending to the serving runtime.

Why this? (intuition)
- Customers frequently trade cost vs latency vs quality; many want predictable tails.
- Small, targeted transforms (compress context, extract instructions, swap to compact model for some tokens, truncate low-value context) can yield big unit savings without product changes.
- Gives product teams an API-exposed knob that is simpler than full model rework.

Hypotheses
- H1: For 60% of queries in our hosted traffic, a cheap pre-transform can reduce token count by >=18% with <=3% downstream regression on quality metrics (measured by eval prompts).
- H2: Allowing customers to attach a per-request SLO profile lets us reduce 95th percentile latency by up to 25% by favoring faster paths, all else equal.

Personas / users
- Frontend engineer at a fintech startup: wants to cap latency to 400ms for chat and reduce cost for low-sensitivity summaries.
- Platform engineer at mid-market company: needs predictable slotting on Dedicated pool; wants ability to force deterministic trimming for budgeted features.
- Internal SRE/ops: wants telemetry to debug sculpt decisions.

Key features (brainstorm list)
- Policy envelope on request: {objective: cost|latency|quality|hybrid, budget: $/req or tokens, fidelity_hint: low|medium|high, privacy_level}
- Transform primitives: compressive summarization of context, anchor extraction (keep last N messages + summary of older), instruction extraction (pull out system instructions to separate short prompt), chunk & stream partial answers, model variant hint (tiny/medium/large), quantization hints, KV-cache reuse hint.
- Progressive request modes: try fast path and fallback to higher-fidelity in background (optimistic return + eventual update) — careful UX needed.
- Preview/simulate API: let customers run sculpting offline and view estimated token savings / quality delta.
- Explainability: per-request reason for changes, diffs of original vs sculpted prompt.

Runtime sketch
- Incoming request -> Scoping -> Heuristics -> Candidate transformations -> Lightweight scoring (estimated tokens, proxy quality score via anchor set) -> Selected transform -> Annotate request with X-headers (sculpted: true, variant: small, reason: anchor-summary-omit) -> send to runtime.
- Keep transforms commutative and reversible where possible (store original in audit log for Private deployments).

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- API: Put a flag: sculpt_profile: {mode: "cost-optim"|"latency-optim"|"none"} + budget_tokens_estimate optional.
- Server returns: sculpted_prompt (for preview), estimated_token_delta, reason_code.
- Telemetry: per-request estimate vs actual token usage, simple QA hooks to fail closed (no sculpt) if proxy estimate uncertain > threshold.
- Performance: end-to-end added latency of sculpting step <= 20ms (most transforms should be <5ms; summarization as async preview).

User stories
- As a product owner, I want to set a default sculpt_profile for a route so we can reduce costs without changing user prompts.
- As an engineer, I want to preview how a sculpt profile changes sample prompts before enabling at scale.
- As an SRE, I want a toggle to opt out of sculpting on Traffic-Restricted Dedicated nodes.

Metrics to track
- Token savings (mean, p50/p95), infer cost delta per route.
- Quality regressions: per-eval-set accuracy, BLEU-like proxies for structured tasks, user-visible delta (e.g., revert rate on optimistic updates).
- Sculpting error rate: % of requests where we aborted sculpt due to uncertainty.
- Latency: additional ms introduced by sculpting layer (p50/p95).

Experiment ideas
- A/B test on low-risk routes: apply anchor-summarizer vs baseline. Measure retention of intent in evals + cost delta.
- Canary with optimistic early-response: return top-1 from fast path immediately and send corrected continuation if fidelity path produces different answer. Measure user confusion and regressions. (dangerous — needs UX guardrails)
- Route-level budget enforcement: when per-route monthly token budget hits X%, start applying aggressive sculpting profile.

Data & eval setup
- Create small eval sets per route: 200 examples with human labels for key tasks (summarization, extraction, code-gen) to measure per-transform regressions.
- Offline simulator: run a corpus through candidate transforms, compute token savings and proxy delta (embedding distance to original response from high-fidelity model).

API sketch (quick)
- POST /v1/generate with body fields: prompt, sculpt_profile: {mode: "latency"|"cost"|"quality", target_tokens: 80, explain: true}
- Headers: X-RI-Sculpt-Seed: <id> to correlate audit logs.
- Response includes: choices + sculpt_meta: {sculpted_prompt, token_delta_estimate, reason_code}

Operational concerns
- Privacy: for Private deployments, do not persist summaries unless customer enables auditing; return-only hooks recommended.
- Security: transformations must not introduce new prompt injection surfaces (e.g., summarizer must not reorder system-guidance into user content).

Notes to self / open questions
- Need a lightweight proxy-quality estimator. Could use small embedding distance model or a distilled classifier. Which? DistilBERT vs tiny embedder? Experiment later.
- How to best present optimistic updates in streaming APIs? Maybe send a flag that the response is "approx" and include an update as separate event if final differs.
- Risk: customers may rely on sculpted output semantics; need explicit opt-in or route-level default with strong explainability.
- Edge-case: multimodal or function-calling flows where sculpting may remove critical function args. Must detect and no-op or enforce strict rules.

Next steps (practical)
- Draft RFC: include API sketch, runtime flow, privacy/opt-out lines. (Put as ticket RI-4521)
- Build small offline tool to run corpus through two transforms: anchor-summarizer and instruction-extractor. Compare token savings and simple scoring. Owner: Liam.
- UX: prototype preview in Console for a single route showing before/after and estimated savings. Owner: Maya.

TODOs
- [ ] Finalize transform primitives list
- [ ] Build offline simulator (Liam)
- [ ] Quick mock endpoint returning sculpted_prompt only for preview (POC)
- [ ] Write a short explainer for Legal re: audit logs and retention

Random brain snippets
- Could piggyback on Optimize's batching suggestions: when a sculpt profile reduces tokens for prediction, update batching heuristics for that route dynamically.
- Consider a simple DSL for sculpt policies for Advanced customers: e.g., keep_last(N=6) + compress_older(k=0.2) + preserve_entities("org_name,email").

End of notes.

(If re-opening after months: re-run offline sim against latest model family; check RI-4521 comments for perf numbers.)
